authority: The exact segment/transport contracts override incidental marks in the illustrative PNG. No drawn track may invent an edge or change mode mid-line.

networks.physicalContinuity: One unbroken sleeper-and-two-rail alignment Valley Halt -> Cogsworth railway platform -> Dust Gulch railway platform. Cogsworth is a through station, not a railway ending in a street.
Separate narrow-gauge track and boarding bay at Gulch; both rails continue to the Caldera landing and end at a buffer. It never becomes the castle footbridge.
Dedicated Cogsworth platform -> supported coastal viaduct -> Skyport platform. No joins to the conventional or mine railway, no continuation as a footpath.
Explicit transfer from Skyport's maglev platform to the lift dock. Separate orbit inset, not railway tracks ascending into clouds.
Two explicit landing pads and a flight line in the inset, not a footpath or rail extension.

interchanges.rule: Same existing service stop ID; distinct drawn railway and maglev platforms connected by a dry forecourt, not a gauge-changing rail junction.
Train ends at buffers. Companion crosses dry station forecourt to a separate mine-cart bay; no vehicle changes mode while moving.
Skyport handles both existing services; a platform-to-dock transfer is not an extension of the maglev track.
Existing shared arrival identity, with separately drawn lift dock/shuttle pad joined by the station's dry corridor.

infrastructureRules.railSurface: Two continuous rails and sleepers to the station's explicit buffer or a declared through-platform. Never fade into dirt, paving or a general road.
infrastructureRules.railBranch: Only a declared same-gauge switch can branch railway track. This design has no unlisted rail branches and no rail-to-maglev switches.
infrastructureRules.tunnels: None are required by this exact schematic. If Claude introduces one for final relief: declare one tunnel ID, two portal anchors, same network/gauge, paired approach headings and a continuous hidden alignment. No lone dark hole standing in for a missing connection.
infrastructureRules.bridges: Declare the carried mode, water/gap beneath, supported deck, abutments and dry approaches. A railway viaduct is not a pedestrian bridge unless it has a separately declared safe foot deck.
infrastructureRules.crossings: Footpath and railway are distinct layers. Use a drawn underpass/overpass, or a separately declared level crossing with clear walk cells; never merge their surfaces. Water may pass beneath a bridge, never onto the walking/rail deck.
infrastructureRules.junctions: Footpaths can join only on dry supported ground. One visible path cannot split into a station teleport or become a vehicle lane.
infrastructureRules.vehiclePresentation: Existing journey rules remain unchanged. The infrastructure is an art/topology specification, not a timetable, fare, simulation or automatic boarding feature.

sea.geometryRule: Entire intermediate route lies in open water. Start/end touch their named piers, never cut across rainforest, waterfall, reef, beach or a lighthouse rock. No track, road or walking continuation across the channel.

acceptance: Trace each named network end to end at full map scale and local scale; no missing segment, unpaired tunnel, free-floating bridge, unsupported cliff turn or unexplained terminus.
Read all junctions without labels: rails, footpaths, guideway and water remain distinct materials and supported layers.
Confirm every station platform joins a reachable dry walking node and every rail terminal has a buffer or its explicit non-rail dock type.
When final terrain requires a tunnel, bridge or level crossing, add its exact semantic anchors before drawing details. This graph does not certify those future pixels.
Do not send the illustrative PNG as a production-ready route mask. Final Claude art must pass a second route-continuity review against these contracts.
